scene.metaphor: An obscure vision model is a hand-built, finicky little machine being lifted out of a cluttered workshop and set onto a clean GPU pedestal, like a temperamental appliance turned into a paid service.
scene.setting: A polished studio tabletop built as a miniature tech workshop: cool-gray surface, soft shadowed backdrop, one clean cobalt pedestal on the right, a messy but contained tool cluster on the left, lots of negative space above.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal is mid-action, calmly pressing a small toggle as the tiny model unit is already gliding from the messy bench onto the pedestal, with one cable still half-tangled in the old setup like it reluctantly came along.
physical_materials: 3D-printed vision-model box with a lens-like front
a single restrained warm amber indicator light
scene.image_instruction: Create a polished studio photograph of Tal Perry as a recognizable, relaxed operator: dark curly hair, salt-and-pepper beard, warm smile, wearing a coral/orange sleeveless athletic tank. He stands in a miniature cool-gray workshop set, framed wide for a 3:1 banner with generous negative space and the action running laterally. On the left, a small cluttered bench holds one obscure vision machine made literal as a compact 3D-printed box with a lens front, tiny cables, and a few scattered tool scraps. On the right, a clean cobalt pedestal awaits it like a remote GPU host. Freeze the absurd instant where Tal, with one hand and a calm deadpan expression, is guiding the little machine off the messy bench toward the pedestal while a thin black cable remains half-tangled behind it. Use polished studio lighting, high tonal separation, cool-gray foundation, cobalt and mint accents, and only one restrained amber status light. Keep a thick simple silhouette and one dominant subject so the joke reads clearly at thumbnail size.
